subject: EU-WEST service degradation — executive summary and immediate next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ruiz <sruiz@heliomed.com>, Alex Choi <alex.choi@greenline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: EU-WEST service degradation — executive summary and immediate next steps

Samantha / Alex —

I wanted to make sure you had an executive-level note as we stand up the incident bridge. We are seeing elevated 5xx errors and request timeouts from instances serving the EU-WEST region starting ~08:48 UTC. Impact: token-generation requests are intermittently failing or timing out for customers pinned to EU-WEST; global failover to other regions has been applied for most routing rules but we know HelioMed has a region pin for latency-sensitive traffic.

What we're doing right now:
- Incident bridge established (Zoom: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210) — engineering and networking on the call.
- Traffic mitigation: we have enabled cross-region routing for eligible endpoints and increased autoscaler headroom on dedicated pools.
- Initial rollback: a recent scheduler change is being reverted on a small canary set to test stability.
- Customer-facing metrics and timeline attached (incident-timeline-v0.pdf, service-metrics-euwest.csv).

Immediate asks from you:
- Please confirm whether HelioMed is currently pinned to EU-WEST (I see a policy indicating yes) and whether you can accept temporary cross-region routing for the next 4 hours.
- Share any critical scheduled jobs or demos today that absolutely must remain in EU-WEST.

I will send one consolidated update at the top of every hour and an executive summary when we have a confirmed mitigation or ETA for full restoration. If you'd like a dedicated exec bridge, we'll be on the line.

Sincere apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your users.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Operations | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachment: incident-timeline-v0.pdf

From: Samantha Ruiz <sruiz@heliomed.com>

Date: 2027-06-01T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: EU-WEST service degradation — executive summary and immediate next steps

Karthik —

We are seeing a spike in failed API calls that started around 08:50 UTC; several patient-facing flows are degrading. We are pinned to EU-WEST for regulatory reasons for a subset of traffic (PHI tokenization endpoint). Cross-region routing is not currently approved for PHI workflows.

Short questions:
1) How long before you can confirm whether the scheduler rollback stabilizes the cluster?
2) Is there a targeted ETA to restore normal 200s for the PHI endpoints or a temporary mitigation that doesn't move PHI off-region?

We appreciate the hourly updates — please loop in security/compliance if cross-region work is proposed.

Thanks,
Samantha Ruiz
Head of Platform Engineering | HelioMed
sruiz@heliomed.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Ruiz <sruiz@heliomed.com>, Alex Choi <alex.choi@greenline.ai>
Date: 2027-06-01T11:30:00Z
Subject: RE: EU-WEST service degradation — engineering update and mitigation applied

Team / HelioMed —

Quick technical update from the bridge:
- Root signal: elevated scheduler queue latency correlated with a recently deployed change to the multi-tenant scheduler (deploy at 08:42 UTC). The scheduler's backpressure logic failed to prioritize reclamation on certain GPU pools, causing sustained queue growth and sporadic OOM-driven restarts.
- Actions taken: rolled back scheduler change on canary pools at 10:05 UTC; increased eviction thresholds and cleared the stalled queue segments; burst autoscale added +6 nodes to EU-WEST at 10:18 UTC.
- Status: error rate has dropped ~70% on the canary set; global cross-region routing applied for non-PHI customers. For PHI-pinned traffic, we are keeping that traffic pinned and applying in-region mitigations only.
- Next steps: keep the canary under observation for 60 minutes; if stable we'll promote rollback cluster-wide. Postmortem ticket created: INF-9123. I've attached the raw metrics export (service-metrics-euwest.csv).

We are prioritizing HelioMed's PHI endpoints; Monica is coordinating with Security to validate any temporary mitigation that might touch PVs.

Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Runtime Reliability | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: service-metrics-euwest.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ruiz <sruiz@heliomed.com>, Alex Choi <alex.choi@greenline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T13:45:00Z
Subject: Executive summary: EU-WEST incident, suspected cause, and customer commitments

Samantha / Alex —

Thanks for the quick responses and for the patience while our engineering teams worked through mitigations. Below is an executive summary you can share internally.

What happened
- A scheduler change deployed at 08:42 UTC produced unintended backpressure behavior in the multi-tenant scheduler, which in turn caused queue growth and memory pressure on several EU-WEST GPU pools. This manifested as intermittent 5xx errors and timeouts for token-generation requests.

Impact
- HelioMed: partial impact to PHI-pinned endpoints for approximately 08:48–11:00 UTC with degraded success rates; non-PHI traffic saw larger-scale impact until cross-region routing mitigations were applied.

What we did
- Immediately rolled back the scheduler change on canary pools at 10:05 UTC and observed a 70% reduction in errors on canary traffic.
- Applied burst autoscaling and eviction threshold adjustments to reduce OOM restarts.
- For PHI-pinned traffic, we did not change region routing; instead we prioritized in-region headroom and queue clearing to maintain compliance.

Customer commitments (HelioMed)
- Hourly status updates until metrics normalize. Next update at 14:45 UTC.
- Dedicated post-incident call scheduled tomorrow 2027-06-02 16:00 UTC to walk through the timeline and remediation plan; invite attached (postmortem-invite.ics).
- Root-cause postmortem (INF-9123) and proposed scheduler hardening plan will be shared within 72 hours.
- We will provide a goodwill credit against June usage for impacted capacity; Ben will follow up with finance and contract team.

Immediate asks for HelioMed
- Confirmation that in-region mitigations are acceptable for PHI endpoints (we will not move PHI off-region without written approval).
- Any additional logs or correlation IDs you can share with Marissa will help accelerate the timeline.

We are sincerely sorry for the disruption. We understand the sensitivity of PHI traffic and are coordinating with Security and Compliance on every proposed mitigation. If you'd like a short exec call now (30 min) I can join.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Operations | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Attachment: postmortem-invite.ics
